    35	/** stdout must be exactly one parseable envelope line. */
    36	function theEnvelope(io) {
    37	  const out = io.stdoutText().trim();
    38	  const lines = out === '' ? [] : out.split('\n');
    39	  assert.equal(lines.length, 1, `expected exactly one stdout line, got: ${JSON.stringify(io.stdoutText())}`);
    40	  const env = JSON.parse(lines[0]);
    41	  for (const k of ['ok', 'data', 'warnings', 'error']) assert.ok(k in env, `envelope carries ${k}`);
    42	  return env;
    43	}

   391	   171	describe('validateLoopSpec — rejections (each error names the offender)', () => {
   392	   172	  const bad = (over, needle) => {
   393	   173	    const { validateLoopSpec } = M();
   394	   174	    const r = validateLoopSpec(validSpec(over), fullConfig());
   395	   175	    assert.equal(r.ok, false, `expected rejection for ${JSON.stringify(over)}`);
   396	   176	    assert.ok(Array.isArray(r.errors) && r.errors.length > 0, 'errors is a non-empty array');
   397	   177	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => new RegExp(needle).test(e)), `an error mentions ${needle}; got ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
   398	   178	  };
   399	   179	
   400	   180	  it('wrong schema', () => bad({ schema: 'baton/loop@2' }, 'schema'));
   401	   181	  it('missing schema', () => bad({ schema: undefined }, 'schema'));
   402	   182	  it('missing goal', () => bad({ goal: undefined }, 'goal'));
   403	   183	  it('empty goal', () => bad({ goal: '' }, 'goal'));
   404	   184	  it('phases not an array', () => bad({ phases: 'nope' }, 'phases'));
   405	   185	  it('phases empty', () => bad({ phases: [] }, 'phases'));
   406	   186	  it('a phase missing id', () => bad({ phases: [{ role: 'planner' }] }, 'id'));
   407	   187	  it('a phase missing role', () => bad({ phases: [{ id: 'x' }] }, 'role'));
   408	   188	
   409	   189	  it("a phase role not in config.roles reports \"unknown role '<id>'\"", () => {
   410	   190	    const { validateLoopSpec } = M();
   411	   191	    const r = validateLoopSpec(validSpec({ phases: [{ id: 'plan', role: 'planner' }, { id: 'x', role: 'ghost-role' }] }), fullConfig());
   412	   192	    assert.equal(r.ok, false);
   413	   193	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => e.includes("unknown role 'ghost-role'")), `got ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
   414	   194	  });
   415	   195	
   416	   196	  it("the unknown-role check fires against a config MISSING a referenced role", () => {
   417	   197	    const { defaultLoopSpec, validateLoopSpec } = M();
   418	   198	    const cfg = fullConfig();
   419	   199	    delete cfg.roles['subtask-reviewer']; // the default spec references it
   420	   200	    const r = validateLoopSpec(defaultLoopSpec('g'), cfg);
   421	   201	    assert.equal(r.ok, false);
   422	   202	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => e.includes("unknown role 'subtask-reviewer'")), `got ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
   423	   203	  });
   424	   204	
   425	   205	  it('budgets.iterationCap missing (budgets present, cap absent)', () => bad({ budgets: { perRoleTimeoutMin: 30, maxChildrenPerPhase: 10 } }, 'iterationCap'));
   426	   206	  it('budgets.iterationCap non-number', () => bad({ budgets: { iterationCap: 'five', perRoleTimeoutMin: 30, maxChildrenPerPhase: 10 } }, 'iterationCap'));
   427	   207	  it('budgets.iterationCap < 1', () => bad({ budgets: { iterationCap: 0, perRoleTimeoutMin: 30, maxChildrenPerPhase: 10 } }, 'iterationCap'));
   428	   208	
   429	   209	  it('budgets.iterationCap > 5 is INVALID — the 5-cap is a hard invariant', () => {
   430	   210	    const { validateLoopSpec } = M();
   431	   211	    const r = validateLoopSpec(validSpec({ budgets: { iterationCap: 6, perRoleTimeoutMin: 30, maxChildrenPerPhase: 10 } }), fullConfig());
   432	   212	    assert.equal(r.ok, false, 'a spec asking for a 6th iteration must be rejected');
   433	   213	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => /iterationCap/.test(e)), `got ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
   434	   214	  });
   435	   215	
   436	   216	  it('smoke present but cmd not string-or-null', () => bad({ smoke: { cmd: 123, expect: null } }, 'cmd|smoke'));
   437	   217	  it('smoke present but expect not string-or-null', () => bad({ smoke: { cmd: null, expect: 7 } }, 'expect|smoke'));
   438	   218	
   439	   219	  it('reports ALL problems at once, not just the first', () => {
   440	   220	    const { validateLoopSpec } = M();
   441	   221	    const r = validateLoopSpec(
   442	   222	      validSpec({ schema: 'wrong', goal: '', budgets: { iterationCap: 6, perRoleTimeoutMin: 30, maxChildrenPerPhase: 10 } }),
   443	   223	      fullConfig(),
   444	   224	    );
   445	   225	    assert.equal(r.ok, false);
   446	   226	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => /schema/.test(e)), 'schema error present');
   447	   227	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => /goal/.test(e)), 'goal error present');
   448	   228	    assert.ok(r.errors.some((/** @type {string} */ e) => /iterationCap/.test(e)), 'iterationCap error present');
   449	   229	    assert.ok(r.errors.length >= 3, `all three problems reported; got ${JSON.stringify(r.errors)}`);
   450	   230	  });

  2350	    27	/**
  2351	    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
  2352	    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
  2353	    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
  2354	    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
  2355	    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
  2356	    33	 * @returns {string}
  2357	    34	 */
  2358	    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
  2359	    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
  2360	    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
  2361	    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
  2362	    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
  2363	    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
  2364	    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
  2365	    42	  let dir = start;
  2366	    43	  while (true) {
  2367	    44	    try {
  2368	    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
  2369	    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
  2370	    47	    } catch {
  2371	    48	      break;
  2372	    49	    }
  2373	    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
  2374	    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
  2375	    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
  2376	    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
  2377	    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
  2378	    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
  2379	    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
  2380	    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
  2381	    58	        dir = driveRoot;
  2382	    59	        continue;
  2383	    60	      }
  2384	    61	      break;
  2385	    62	    }
  2386	    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
  2387	    64	    dir = parent;
  2388	    65	  }
  2389	    66	  return start;
  2390	    67	}

  2422	    99	/**
  2423	   100	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
  2424	   101	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
  2425	   102	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
  2426	   103	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
  2427	   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
  2428	   105	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
  2429	   106	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
  2430	   107	 * @param {string[]} args
  2431	   108	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
  2432	   109	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
  2433	   110	 */
  2434	   111	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
  2435	   112	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
  2436	   113	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
  2437	   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  2438	   115	  const flags = {};
  2439	   116	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
  2440	   117	    const a = args[i];
  2441	   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
  2442	   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
  2443	   120	    const kind = full[key];
  2444	   121	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
  2445	   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
  2446	   123	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
  2447	   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
  2448	   125	      const next = args[i + 1];
  2449	   126	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
  2450	   127	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
  2451	   128	      }
  2452	   129	      flags[key] = true;
  2453	   130	      continue;
  2454	   131	    }
  2455	   132	    const next = args[i + 1];
  2456	   133	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
  2457	   134	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
  2458	   135	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
  2459	   136	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
  2460	   137	    }
  2461	   138	    flags[key] = next;
  2462	   139	    i += 1;
  2463	   140	  }
  2464	   141	  return { flags };
  2465	   142	}
  2466	   143	
  2467	   144	/**
  2468	   145	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
  2469	   146	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
  2470	   147	 * @param {string[]} args
  2471	   148	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
  2472	   149	 */
  2473	   150	export function parseFlags(args) {
  2474	   151	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  2475	   152	  const flags = {};
  2476	   153	  /** @type {string[]} */
  2477	   154	  const positionals = [];
  2478	   155	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
  2479	   156	    const a = args[i];
  2480	   157	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
  2481	   158	      const key = a.slice(2);
  2482	   159	      const next = args[i + 1];
  2483	   160	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
  2484	   161	        flags[key] = next;
  2485	   162	        i += 1;
  2486	   163	      } else {
  2487	   164	        flags[key] = true;
  2488	   165	      }
  2489	   166	    } else {
  2490	   167	      positionals.push(a);
  2491	   168	    }
  2492	   169	  }
  2493	   170	  return { flags, positionals };
  2494	   171	}

  2722	     9	  e.code = code;
  2723	    10	  e.syscall = syscall;

  2728	    15	function normalize(p) {
  2729	    16	  const str = String(p);
  2730	    17	  const isAbs = str.startsWith('/');
  2731	    18	  const out = [];
  2732	    19	  for (const part of str.split('/')) {
  2733	    20	    if (part === '' || part === '.') continue;
  2734	    21	    if (part === '..') {
  2735	    22	      out.pop();
  2736	    23	      continue;
  2737	    24	    }
  2738	    25	    out.push(part);
  2739	    26	  }
  2740	    27	  return (isAbs ? '/' : '') + out.join('/');
  2741	    28	}

  2753	    40	export function makeMemfs(initialFiles = {}) {
  2754	    41	  const store = new Map(); // path -> string content
  2755	    42	  const dirs = new Set(['/']);
  2756	    43	  const mtimes = new Map();
  2757	    44	  const history = [];
  2758	    45	  let clock = 0;
  2759	    46	
  2760	    47	  const snapshot = () => Object.fromEntries(store);
  2761	    48	  const record = (op, paths) => history.push({ op, paths, files: snapshot() });
  2762	    49	  const touch = (np) => mtimes.set(np, ++clock);
  2763	    50	
  2764	    51	  const mkdirp = (np) => {
  2765	    52	    let cur = '';
  2766	    53	    for (const part of np.split('/').filter(Boolean)) {
  2767	    54	      cur = cur + '/' + part;
  2768	    55	      dirs.add(cur);
  2769	    56	    }
  2770	    57	  };
  2771	    58	
  2772	    59	  const ensureParent = (np, syscall) => {
  2773	    60	    const parent = dirname(np);
  2774	    61	    if (parent === '/' ) return;
  2775	    62	    if (!dirs.has(parent)) throw fsError('ENOENT', syscall, np);
  2776	    63	  };
  2777	    64	
  2778	    65	  for (const [p, content] of Object.entries(initialFiles)) {
  2779	    66	    const np = normalize(p);
  2780	    67	    mkdirp(dirname(np));
  2781	    68	    store.set(np, String(content));

  2783	    70	  }
  2784	    71	
  2785	    72	  const fs = {
  2786	    73	    readFileSync(p /*, enc */) {
  2787	    74	      const np = normalize(p);
  2788	    75	      if (!store.has(np)) throw fsError('ENOENT', 'open', np);
  2789	    76	      return store.get(np);
  2790	    77	    },
  2791	    78	
  2792	    79	    writeFileSync(p, data /*, enc */) {
  2793	    80	      const np = normalize(p);
  2794	    81	      ensureParent(np, 'open');
  2795	    82	      store.set(np, String(data));
  2796	    83	      touch(np);
  2797	    84	      record('writeFileSync', [np]);
  2798	    85	    },
  2799	    86	
  2800	    87	    appendFileSync(p, data) {
  2801	    88	      const np = normalize(p);
  2802	    89	      ensureParent(np, 'open');
  2803	    90	      store.set(np, (store.get(np) || '') + String(data));
  2804	    91	      touch(np);
  2805	    92	      record('appendFileSync', [np]);
  2806	    93	    },
  2807	    94	
  2808	    95	    renameSync(from, to) {

  2810	    97	      const nt = normalize(to);
  2811	    98	      if (store.has(nf)) {

  2814	   101	        store.delete(nf);

  2819	   106	      }

  2821	   108	      // lock's dead-reclaim arbitration renames the stale lock dir aside.

  2830	   117	            store.delete(k);
  2831	   118	          }
  2832	   119	        }
  2833	   120	        for (const d of [...dirs]) {

  2835	   122	            dirs.add(nt + d.slice(nf.length));

  5057	     1	/**
  5058	     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
  5059	     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
  5060	     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
  5061	     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
  5062	     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
  5063	     7	 */
  5064	     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
  5065	     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
  5066	    10	  const notes = [];
  5067	    11	
  5068	    12	  /**
  5069	    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
  5070	    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
  5071	    15	   */
  5072	    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
  5073	    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
  5074	    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
  5075	    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
  5076	    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
  5077	    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
  5078	    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
  5079	    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
  5080	    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
  5081	    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
  5082	    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
  5083	    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
  5084	    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
  5085	    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
  5086	    30	    }
  5087	    31	    return null;
  5088	    32	  }
  5089	    33	
  5090	    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
  5091	    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
  5092	    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
  5093	    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
  5094	    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
  5095	    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
  5096	    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
  5097	    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
  5098	    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
  5099	    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
  5100	    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
  5101	    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
  5102	    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
  5103	    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
  5104	    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
  5105	    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
  5106	    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
  5107	    51	  };
  5108	    52	
  5109	    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
  5110	    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
  5111	    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
  5112	    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
  5113	    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
  5114	    58	  /** @param {any} m */
  5115	    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
  5116	    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
  5117	    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>
  5118	    62	    avoidEntries.some((a) => a?.platform === platform && baseModel(a?.model) === baseModel(model));
  5119	    63	
  5120	    64	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
  5121	    65	  const assignments = {};
  5122	    66	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
  5123	    67	    /** @type {any[]} */
  5124	    68	    const skipped = [];
  5125	    69	    /** @type {any} */
  5126	    70	    let assignment = null;
  5127	    71	
  5128	    72	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
  5129	    73	      const entry = chain[i];
  5130	    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
  5131	    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
  5132	    76	        continue;
  5133	    77	      }
  5134	    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
  5135	    79	      if (why) {
  5136	    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
  5137	    81	        continue;
  5138	    82	      }
  5139	    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
  5140	    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
  5141	    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
  5142	    86	        continue;
  5143	    87	      }
  5144	    88	      assignment = {
  5145	    89	        platform: entry.platform,
  5146	    90	        model: entry.model,
  5147	    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
  5148	    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
  5149	    93	        chainIndex: i,
  5150	    94	        skipped,
  5151	    95	      };
  5152	    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
  5153	    97	      break;
  5154	    98	    }
  5155	    99	
  5156	   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
  5157	   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
  5158	   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
  5159	   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
  5160	   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
  5161	   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
  5162	   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
  5163	   107	      }
  5164	   108	    }
  5165	   109	
  5166	   110	    if (!assignment) {
  5167	   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
  5168	   112	    }
  5169	   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
  5170	   114	  }
  5171	   115	
  5172	   116	  return { assignments, notes };

  5289	docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:56:**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
  5290	docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:60:**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.

  5545	   142	
  5546	   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
  5547	   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
  5548	   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
  5549	   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
  5550	   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
  5551	   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
  5552	   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
  5553	   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
  5554	   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
  5555	   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
  5556	   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
  5557	   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.

  5561	   158	  groups reaped on adoption).

  5566	   163	  approves it → implementer writes only enough to pass it — the repo TDD

  5568	   165	  runs `smoke.cmd`, records output, and STOPS, writing

  7880	  2242	    33	### Loop spec
  7881	  2243	    34	
  7882	  2244	    35	`loop.json` at repo root (schema `baton/loop@1`), scaffolded by
  7883	  2245	    36	`baton loop init "<goal>"`:
  7884	  2246	    37

  7900	  2262	    53	### Role-matrix additions (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 1)
  7901	  2263	    54	
  7902	  2264	    55	The loop references roles by ID only; every referenced role must exist in the
  7903	  2265	    56	matrix or `loop.json` validation fails (`unknown role '<id>'`, exit 2, before
  7904	  2266	    57	any child spawns). Four roles are ADDED to `baton.config.json` +
  7905	  2267	    58	`templates/baton.config.json.tpl` in the first implementation task:
  7906	  2268	    59	
  7907	  2269	    60	- `subtask-reviewer` — per-subtask diff review inside the loop cycle.
  7908	  2270	    61	- `merger` — the only role that writes main in pipeline mode; adversarial
  7909	  2271	    62	  re-check before merge.
  7910	  2272	    63	- `worker-a`, `worker-b` — the two pipeline seats. Subtask N assigns
  7911	  2273	    64	  writer = seat (N mod 2), reviewer = the other seat; the SEATS swap, and each
  7912	  2274	    65	  seat's concrete platform/model comes from its configured chain via the
  7913	  2275	    66	  resolver. No vendor or model name appears in this plan, child prompts, or
  7914	  2276	    67	  loop code — chains live in config only.
  7915	  2277	    68	
  7916	  2278	    69	### `baton loop` (Layer 2)
  7917	  2279	    70	
  7918	  2280	    71	- `baton loop init <goal>` — scaffold spec + plan template; idempotent,
  7919	  2281	    72	  dry-run-able, same two-phase plan/apply discipline as `baton init`.
  7920	  2282	    73	- `baton loop run [--approve-smoke <token>]` — the state machine. State lives
  7921	  2283	    74	  in gitignored `.handoff/loop/state.json` + `journal.ndjson` (same atomic
  7922	  2284	    75	  write + journal replay machinery as the bundle; loop position is also
  7923	  2285	    76	  checkpointed into the handoff bundle so a limit death carries it).
  7924	  2286	    77	
  7925	  2287	    78	### Root + ownership discipline (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 2)
  7926	  2288	    79	
  7927	  2289	    80	One authoritative root: the MAIN repo root where `loop.json` lives. The
  7928	  2290	    81	supervisor is the SOLE writer of `.handoff/loop/` and of the main root's
  7929	  2291	    82	handoff bundle; every supervisor-driven baton invocation passes explicit
  7930	  2292	    83	`--root <mainRoot>` and a supervisor-owned stable session hint
  7931	  2293	    84	(`--session loop-<runId>` — a NEW flag added to `checkpoint`; `receive`
  7932	  2294	    85	already has it), so the bundle has exactly one stable owner.
  7933	  2295	    86	
  7934	  2296	    87	**Child-hook policy (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 1; iteration 3,
  7935	  2297	    88	finding 1)** — children never touch OR read any bundle, by construction: the
  7936	  2298	    89	supervisor sets `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1` in every child's environment, and
  7937	  2299	    90	EVERY baton hook command — the hook entrypoints, `baton checkpoint`, and
  7938	  2300	    91	`baton session-start` (which would otherwise read the bundle and inject
  7939	  2301	    92	pending-handoff resume context into the child) — quietly no-ops (exit 0,
  7940	  2302	    93	empty output) when it is set. This covers
  7941	  2303	    94	Layer-2 children running in the MAIN root (where root discovery would
  7942	  2304	    95	otherwise find the supervisor-owned bundle and the foreign-session guard
  7943	  2305	    96	would reject their stable hints) and pipeline children in worktrees alike;
  7944	  2306	    97	narrative checkpointing for supervised work is the supervisor's job, driven
  7945	  2307	    98	by parsed child results. Contract tests: (a) Layer-2 — two concurrent
  7946	  2308	    99	main-root children with distinct stable session hints and live hooks →
  7947	  2309	   100	zero bundle mutations, zero foreign-session rejections, supervisor
  7948	  2310	   101	`--session` checkpoints land; (b) pipeline — same from two worktrees while
  7949	  2311	   102	the supervisor writes loop state.
  7950	  2312	   103	- Each role invocation is a headless child under the supervisor:
  7951	  2313	   104	  - claude-code roles: `claude -p "<role prompt>" --permission-mode
  7952	  2314	   105	    acceptEdits --allowedTools ...` (allowlist per role: reviewers read-only).

  7954	  2316	   107	    model_reasoning_effort=<e> "<prompt>" </dev/null` (stdin closed — the
  7955	  2317	   108	    stdin-hang class is a known field failure).
  7956	  2318	   109	  - Verdict contract: children end with the structured tail

  8007	  2369	    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
  8008	  2370	    47	    } catch {

  8065	  2427	   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token

  8075	  2437	   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  8076	  2438	   115	  const flags = {};

  8078	  2440	   117	    const a = args[i];
  8079	  2441	   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
  8080	  2442	   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
  8081	  2443	   120	    const kind = full[key];

  8083	  2445	   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {

  8085	  2447	   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
  8086	  2448	   125	      const next = args[i + 1];

  8090	  2452	   129	      flags[key] = true;
  8091	  2453	   130	      continue;

  8093	  2455	   132	    const next = args[i + 1];

  8098	  2460	   137	    }

  8100	  2462	   139	    i += 1;

  8397	  2759	    46	
  8398	  2760	    47	  const snapshot = () => Object.fromEntries(store);
  8399	  2761	    48	  const record = (op, paths) => history.push({ op, paths, files: snapshot() });
  8400	  2762	    49	  const touch = (np) => mtimes.set(np, ++clock);

  8414	  2776	    63	  };

 10928	  5290	docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:60:**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker.  11182	  5544	   141	"Survives the operator's session ending" is a defined mechanism, not a hope:
 11183	  5545	   142	
 11184	  5546	   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
 11185	  5547	   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
 11186	  5548	   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
 11187	  5549	   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
 11188	  5550	   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
 11189	  5551	   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
 11190	  5552	   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
 11191	  5553	   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
 11192	  5554	   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
 11193	  5555	   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
 11194	  5556	   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
 11195	  5557	   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.
 11196	  5558	   155	- Acceptance adds a supervisor-death test: kill the supervisor (and its
 11197	  5559	   156	  launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
 11198	  5560	   157	  journal and continues or parks; no orphaned children survive (process
 11199	  5561	   158	  groups reaped on adoption).

    48	/**
    49	 * The --json contract: exactly one compact envelope line on stdout, nothing else.
    50	 * @param {any} io
    51	 * @param {{ok: boolean, data?: any, warnings?: any[], error?: {code: string, msg: string} | null}} env
    52	 */
    53	function emitEnvelope(io, env) {
    54	  const full = { ok: env.ok, data: env.data ?? null, warnings: env.warnings ?? [], error: env.error ?? null };
    55	  io.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(full) + '\n');
    56	}
    57	
    58	/**
    59	 * @param {string[]} argv process args after the binary
    60	 * @param {any} io injected {cwd, stdout, stderr}
    61	 * @returns {number | Promise<number>} exit code
    62	 */
    63	export function run(argv, io) {
    64	  const args = argv.filter((a) => a !== '');
    65	  // Global --json intent is parsed BEFORE dispatch (gate-2 iter-2 M6): a
    66	  // top-level `--json` with no command, or --help/--version, must still emit
    67	  // exactly one envelope rather than raw text.
    68	  const jsonWanted = args.includes('--json');
    69	  const cmdIndex = args.findIndex((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
    70	  const cmd = cmdIndex === -1 ? undefined : args[cmdIndex];
    71	
    72	  if (cmd === undefined) {
    73	    // No command — just flags (or nothing).
    74	    if (args.includes('--version')) {
    75	      if (jsonWanted) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { version: version() } });
    76	      else io.stdout.write(version() + '\n');
    77	      return 0;
    78	    }
    79	    if (args.includes('--help')) {
    80	      if (jsonWanted) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { usage: USAGE.trim() } });
    81	      else io.stdout.write(USAGE);
    82	      return 0;
    83	    }
    84	    // Bare invocation (or a lone --json): a usage error.
    85	    if (jsonWanted) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'usage', msg: 'no command given' } });
    86	    else io.stdout.write(USAGE);
    87	    return 2;
    88	  }
    89	
    90	  // All flags (before and after the command token) reach the command; only the
    91	  // command token itself is stripped, so a leading `--json` isn't lost.
    92	  const rest = args.filter((_, i) => i !== cmdIndex);
    93	
    94	  // Usage errors honor the --json envelope contract too (gate-2 fix 11 + M6:
    95	  // global --json counts, wherever it sits).
    96	  const wantsJson = jsonWanted;
    97	  if (cmd === 'wrap') {
    98	    if (wantsJson) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'usage', msg: 'baton wrap is reserved for a future release (PTY supervisor); not available in v1' } });
    99	    else io.stderr.write(`baton wrap is reserved for a future release (PTY supervisor); not available in v1.\n${USAGE}`);
   100	    return 2;
   101	  }
   102	  if (!COMMANDS.includes(cmd)) {
   103	    if (wantsJson) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'usage', msg: `unknown command '${cmd}'` } });
   104	    else io.stderr.write(`baton: unknown command '${cmd}'\n${USAGE}`);
   105	    return 2;
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  if (rest.includes('--help')) {
   109	    // Subcommand help honors the global --json envelope too (iter-3 F8): with

    27	/**
    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
    33	 * @returns {string}
    34	 */
    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
    42	  let dir = start;
    43	  while (true) {
    44	    try {
    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
    47	    } catch {
    48	      break;
    49	    }
    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
    58	        dir = driveRoot;
    59	        continue;
    60	      }
    61	      break;
    62	    }
    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
    64	    dir = parent;
    65	  }
    66	  return start;
    67	}

    99	/**
   100	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
   101	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
   102	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
   103	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
   105	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
   106	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
   107	 * @param {string[]} args
   108	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
   109	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
   110	 */
   111	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
   112	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
   113	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   115	  const flags = {};
   116	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   117	    const a = args[i];
   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
   120	    const kind = full[key];
   121	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
   123	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
   125	      const next = args[i + 1];
   126	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   127	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
   128	      }
   129	      flags[key] = true;
   130	      continue;
   131	    }
   132	    const next = args[i + 1];
   133	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
   134	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
   135	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
   136	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
   137	    }
   138	    flags[key] = next;
   139	    i += 1;
   140	  }
   141	  return { flags };
   142	}
   143	
   144	/**
   145	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
   146	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
   147	 * @param {string[]} args
   148	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
   149	 */
   150	export function parseFlags(args) {
   151	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   152	  const flags = {};
   153	  /** @type {string[]} */
   154	  const positionals = [];
   155	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   156	    const a = args[i];
   157	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
   158	      const key = a.slice(2);
   159	      const next = args[i + 1];
   160	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   161	        flags[key] = next;
   162	        i += 1;
   163	      } else {
   164	        flags[key] = true;
   165	      }
   166	    } else {
   167	      positionals.push(a);
   168	    }
   169	  }
   170	  return { flags, positionals };
   171	}

    15	function normalize(p) {
    16	  const str = String(p);
    17	  const isAbs = str.startsWith('/');
    18	  const out = [];
    19	  for (const part of str.split('/')) {
    20	    if (part === '' || part === '.') continue;
    21	    if (part === '..') {
    22	      out.pop();
    23	      continue;
    24	    }
    25	    out.push(part);
    26	  }
    27	  return (isAbs ? '/' : '') + out.join('/');
    28	}

    40	export function makeMemfs(initialFiles = {}) {
    41	  const store = new Map(); // path -> string content
    42	  const dirs = new Set(['/']);
    43	  const mtimes = new Map();
    44	  const history = [];
    45	  let clock = 0;
    46	
    47	  const snapshot = () => Object.fromEntries(store);
    48	  const record = (op, paths) => history.push({ op, paths, files: snapshot() });
    49	  const touch = (np) => mtimes.set(np, ++clock);
    50	
    51	  const mkdirp = (np) => {
    52	    let cur = '';
    53	    for (const part of np.split('/').filter(Boolean)) {
    54	      cur = cur + '/' + part;
    55	      dirs.add(cur);
    56	    }
    57	  };
    58	
    59	  const ensureParent = (np, syscall) => {
    60	    const parent = dirname(np);
    61	    if (parent === '/' ) return;
    62	    if (!dirs.has(parent)) throw fsError('ENOENT', syscall, np);
    63	  };
    64	
    65	  for (const [p, content] of Object.entries(initialFiles)) {
    66	    const np = normalize(p);
    67	    mkdirp(dirname(np));
    68	    store.set(np, String(content));
    69	    touch(np);
    70	  }
    71	
    72	  const fs = {
    73	    readFileSync(p /*, enc */) {
    74	      const np = normalize(p);
    75	      if (!store.has(np)) throw fsError('ENOENT', 'open', np);
    76	      return store.get(np);
    77	    },
    78	
    79	    writeFileSync(p, data /*, enc */) {
    80	      const np = normalize(p);
    81	      ensureParent(np, 'open');
    82	      store.set(np, String(data));
    83	      touch(np);
    84	      record('writeFileSync', [np]);
    85	    },
    86	
    87	    appendFileSync(p, data) {
    88	      const np = normalize(p);
    89	      ensureParent(np, 'open');
    90	      store.set(np, (store.get(np) || '') + String(data));
    91	      touch(np);
    92	      record('appendFileSync', [np]);
    93	    },
    94	
    95	    renameSync(from, to) {
    96	      const nf = normalize(from);
    97	      const nt = normalize(to);
    98	      if (store.has(nf)) {
    99	        ensureParent(nt, 'rename');
   100	        const content = store.get(nf);
   101	        store.delete(nf);
   102	        store.set(nt, content);
   103	        touch(nt);
   104	        record('renameSync', [nf, nt]);
   105	        return;
   106	      }
   107	      // Directory rename (atomic move of the node and all descendants) — the
   108	      // lock's dead-reclaim arbitration renames the stale lock dir aside.
   109	      if (dirs.has(nf)) {
   110	        ensureParent(nt, 'rename');
   111	        const pre = nf + '/';
   112	        dirs.delete(nf);
   113	        dirs.add(nt);
   114	        for (const k of [...store.keys()]) {
   115	          if (k.startsWith(pre)) {
   116	            store.set(nt + k.slice(nf.length), store.get(k));
   117	            store.delete(k);
   118	          }
   119	        }
   120	        for (const d of [...dirs]) {
   121	          if (d !== nt && d.startsWith(pre)) {
   122	            dirs.add(nt + d.slice(nf.length));
   123	            dirs.delete(d);
   124	          }
   125	        }
   126	        touch(nt);
   127	        record('renameSync', [nf, nt]);
   128	        return;
   129	      }
   130	      throw fsError('ENOENT', 'rename', nf);
   131	    },
   132	
   133	    mkdirSync(p, opts = {}) {
   134	      const np = normalize(p);
   135	      if (opts.recursive) {
   136	        mkdirp(np);
   137	        record('mkdirSync', [np]);
   138	        return undefined;
   139	      }
   140	      ensureParent(np, 'mkdir');
   141	      if (dirs.has(np) || store.has(np)) throw fsError('EEXIST', 'mkdir', np);
   142	      dirs.add(np);
   143	      record('mkdirSync', [np]);
   144	      return undefined;
   145	    },
   146	
   147	    existsSync(p) {
   148	      const np = normalize(p);
   149	      return store.has(np) || dirs.has(np);
   150	    },
   151	
   152	    readdirSync(p) {
   153	      const np = normalize(p);
   154	      if (!dirs.has(np)) {
   155	        if (store.has(np)) throw fsError('ENOTDIR', 'scandir', np);
   156	        throw fsError('ENOENT', 'scandir', np);
   157	      }
   158	      const names = new Set();
   159	      const collect = (k) => {
   160	        if (k !== np && dirname(k) === np) names.add(basename(k, np));
   161	      };
   162	      for (const k of store.keys()) collect(k);
   163	      for (const d of dirs) collect(d);
   164	      return [...names];
   165	    },
   166	
   167	    unlinkSync(p) {
   168	      const np = normalize(p);
   169	      if (!store.has(np)) throw fsError('ENOENT', 'unlink', np);
   170	      store.delete(np);
   171	      record('unlinkSync', [np]);
   172	    },
   173	
   174	    rmSync(p, opts = {}) {
   175	      const np = normalize(p);
   176	      const isFile = store.has(np);
   177	      const isDir = dirs.has(np);
   178	      if (!isFile && !isDir) {
   179	        if (opts.force) return;
   180	        throw fsError('ENOENT', 'rm', np);
   181	      }
   182	      if (isFile) store.delete(np);
   183	      if (isDir) {
   184	        const pre = np + '/';
   185	        if (!opts.recursive) {
   186	          const hasChildren = [...store.keys(), ...dirs].some((k) => k !== np && k.startsWith(pre));
   187	          if (hasChildren) throw fsError('ENOTEMPTY', 'rmdir', np);
   188	          dirs.delete(np);
   189	        } else {
   190	          for (const k of [...store.keys()]) if (k === np || k.startsWith(pre)) store.delete(k);
   191	          for (const d of [...dirs]) if (d === np || d.startsWith(pre)) dirs.delete(d);
   192	        }
   193	      }
   194	      record('rmSync', [np]);
   195	    },
   196	
   197	    statSync(p) {
   198	      const np = normalize(p);
   199	      if (store.has(np)) {
   200	        const size = Buffer.byteLength(store.get(np));
   201	        return { isFile: () => true, isDirectory: () => false, isSymbolicLink: () => false, size, mtimeMs: mtimes.get(np) || 0 };
   202	      }
   203	      if (dirs.has(np)) {
   204	        return { isFile: () => false, isDirectory: () => true, isSymbolicLink: () => false, size: 0, mtimeMs: mtimes.get(np) || 0 };
   205	      }
   206	      throw fsError('ENOENT', 'stat', np);
   207	    },
   208

   210	    // normalization. Symlink-refusal behavior is proven over the real fs in
   211	    // tests/integration/symlink-escape.test.mjs.
   212	    lstatSync(p) {

 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	// Fake `io` object matching the injected-io contract from docs/design/core.md:
     2	// { cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now }. Backed by memfs.
     3	// stdout/stderr collect writes; io.stdoutText()/io.stderrText() flatten them.
     4	// now() returns a settable ISO string (io.setNow). execFile resolves from an
     5	// execResults map keyed by the joined command string.
     6	//
     7	// Wave-B2 additions (bundle lock layer) — all optional, defaulted, and purely
     8	// additive so no prior consumer is affected:
     9	//   host / pid / startTime  — the process-identity facts the lock model writes
    10	//     into owner.json and compares on contention (see plan §Concurrency, Lock
    11	//     model iterations 3+4).
    12	//   processAlive(pid, startTime) — the "provably dead" oracle. Default: only
    13	//     THIS io's own {pid, startTime} is alive; every other descriptor reads as
    14	//     dead. Override per test to model a live foreign owner or a pid/start-time
    15	//     mismatch (reused pid).
    16	//   newFencingToken() — the injected per-acquisition token source. Deterministic
    17	//     monotonic counter ("tok-1", "tok-2", …), matching the injected-io
    18	//     discipline already used for now()/execFile so lock acquisition is
    19	//     reproducible in tests rather than drawing from Math.random.
    20	
    21	import { makeMemfs } from './memfs.mjs';
    22	
    23	export function makeIo({
    24	  files = {},
    25	  env = {},
    26	  stdin = '',
    27	  execResults = {},
    28	  now = '2026-07-11T00:00:00.000Z',
    29	  host = 'host-A',
    30	  pid = 4242,
    31	  startTime = 111000,
    32	  processAlive = null,
    33	  fencingSeed = 1,
    34	  execPath = process.execPath,
    35	} = {}) {
    36	  const { fs, files: filesSnapshot } = makeMemfs(files);
    37	  const outChunks = [];
    38	  const errChunks = [];
    39	  let currentNow = now;
    40	  let tokenCounter = fencingSeed - 1;
    41	  const defaultAlive = (p, s) => p === pid && s === startTime;
    42	
    43	  const stdout = { write: (s) => { outChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    44	  const stderr = { write: (s) => { errChunks.push(String(s)); return true; } };
    45	
    46	  const execFile = (cmd, args = [], /* opts */ _opts = {}) => {
    47	    const key = [cmd, ...(Array.isArray(args) ? args : [])].join(' ');
    48	    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    49	      if (!(key in execResults)) {
    50	        const e = new Error(`spawn ${cmd} ENOENT`);
    51	        e.code = 'ENOENT';
    52	        return reject(e);
    53	      }
    54	      const r = execResults[key];
    55	      const code = r.code ?? 0;
    56	      const out = r.stdout ?? '';
    57	      const err = r.stderr ?? '';
    58	      if (code !== 0) {
    59	        // util.promisify(execFile) rejects on nonzero exit; error carries code + streams.
    60	        const e = new Error(`Command failed: ${key}`);
    61	        e.code = code;
    62	        e.stdout = out;
    63	        e.stderr = err;
    64	        return reject(e);
    65	      }
    66	      resolve({ stdout: out, stderr: err });
    67	    });
    68	  };
    69	
    70	  return {
    71	    cwd: '/repo',
    72	    env,
    73	    stdin,
    74	    stdout,
    75	    stderr,
    76	    fs,
    77	    execFile,
    78	    now: () => currentNow,
    79	    setNow: (iso) => { currentNow = iso; },
    80	    execPath,
    81	    host,
    82	    pid,
    83	    startTime,
    84	    processAlive: processAlive || defaultAlive,
    85	    // Tiny retry budget: unit tests exercising live-lock refusal stay fast
    86	    // while the retry code path itself still runs (production default: 120x25ms).
    87	    lockRetry: { attempts: 2, delayMs: 2 },
    88	    newFencingToken: () => `tok-${++tokenCounter}`,
    89	    stdoutText: () => outChunks.join(''),
    90	    stderrText: () => errChunks.join(''),
    91	    files: filesSnapshot,
    92	  };
    93	}

    38	- `goal`, `constraints[]` (falsifiable acceptance criteria — the loop's exit
    39	  condition), `smoke` ({cmd, expect} — the staged-gate slice definition),
    40	- `phases` — an ordered list of `{id, role}` entries: `id` is a free label
    41	  for progress display; `role` MUST be a matrix role ID (validation fails on
    42	  any unknown role before a child spawns). Default:
    43	  plan(`planner`) → gate-1(`plan-reviewer`) → smoke — itself a TDD mini-cycle
    44	  per the repo contract: smoke-tests(`test-author`) →
    45	  smoke-verify(`test-verifier`) → smoke-build(`implementer`) → the human
    46	  smoke gate — → per-subtask cycle (`test-author` → `test-verifier` →
    47	  `implementer` → `subtask-reviewer`) → gate-2(`final-reviewer-a`,
    48	  `final-reviewer-b`) → done,
    49	- `budgets` ({iterationCap: 5, perRoleTimeoutMin, maxChildrenPerPhase}),
    50	- roles resolve through the existing `baton.config.json` matrix — never
    51	  hardcoded models.
    52	
    53	### Role-matrix additions (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 1)
    54	
    55	The loop references roles by ID only; every referenced role must exist in the
    56	matrix or `loop.json` validation fails (`unknown role '<id>'`, exit 2, before
    57	any child spawns). Four roles are ADDED to `baton.config.json` +
    58	`templates/baton.config.json.tpl` in the first implementation task:
    59	
    60	- `subtask-reviewer` — per-subtask diff review inside the loop cycle.
    61	- `merger` — the only role that writes main in pipeline mode; adversarial
    62	  re-check before merge.
    63	- `worker-a`, `worker-b` — the two pipeline seats. Subtask N assigns
    64	  writer = seat (N mod 2), reviewer = the other seat; the SEATS swap, and each
    65	  seat's concrete platform/model comes from its configured chain via the
    66	  resolver. No vendor or model name appears in this plan, child prompts, or
    67	  loop code — chains live in config only.
    68	
    69	### `baton loop` (Layer 2)
    70	
    71	- `baton loop init <goal>` — scaffold spec + plan template; idempotent,
    72	  dry-run-able, same two-phase plan/apply discipline as `baton init`.
    73	- `baton loop run [--approve-smoke <token>]` — the state machine. State lives
